_meta.description: Rolling registry of recent post generation characteristics. Used to inject differentiation context into future generation prompts, preventing hook repetition, title cadence cloning, and emotional arc duplication. Capped at 30 recent entries per category.
_meta.usage: Read by scripts/lib/generation-memory.js before generation. Written after each successful post creation. Pass result to generate-post.js as differentiation context.

recentHooks.hook: What if the reason you can't commit isn't that you lack information, but that you're waiting for a guarantee that will never come?

Try this. Right now, count the number of screens, notifications, tabs, and half-finished thoughts fighting for your attention. Then wonder why you can't come up with a single fresh idea.
Here is a thing almost nobody admits out loud: you sit down to make something, and what comes out feels like it was stapled together from parts other people already made.

You've probably rebuilt your morning routine four times this year. The 5am version. The journaling version. The gym-first version. The one with the fancy app that pinged you at sunrise until you turne

Walk into a room with one striking piece on the wall, then walk into the same room after someone takes it down. The second version feels like a sentence with the punctuation removed. Technically fine.
Here's a question worth sitting with: why does your content calendar feel like a second job you never applied for?
A machine wrote a symphony last week that made someone cry, and that person did not know a machine wrote it until later.
Here's a question worth sitting with: when you "handle" your emotions, are you actually moving them through you, or are you just getting really good at not showing them?

Picture two writers with the same deadline, the same skill, the same idea.

Try to read one page of a book right now. Not skim ~ actually read it, hold every sentence in your head, follow the meaning to the bottom of the page. If your eyes slid off the words after two lines a
The busiest week of your life often shows up right before the conversation you don't want to have.

You know that feeling when another artist in your lane drops their third release while you are still exporting stems from the first one? Not because they are more talented. Because they figured out so
Here is the thing nobody warns you about. The piece that lights you up at 11pm during a scroll spiral is not always the piece you will still love hanging over your couch in November.

You automated your captions last month and something felt off, but you couldn't name it. Your posting stayed consistent. Your engagement quietly dropped. And when someone finally replied "this doesn't
Pick up your phone right now and look at the first three apps you open on autopilot. Not the ones you're proud of. The ones your thumb finds before your brain wakes up.
What if the worst decision you made last month was already made before you sat down to decide?

You hit every number you were supposed to hit. The salary, the title, the house with the good light in the mornings. And then one ordinary Tuesday, driving home from a job you are supposedly great at,
Here's the thing nobody says out loud: you will never see the end of it before you start. Not the good version, not the honest version, not the one worth doing.

You told yourself you'd drink water first thing. You didn't. You told yourself you'd stretch for five minutes, journal one line, put your phone across the room at night. You didn't. And now there's th

You white-knuckle your way through the morning, feel like a monk by noon, and by 11pm you are three hours deep into a feed you do not even remember opening. Sound familiar?

Take everything off one wall in your home. Just for a second. Notice how the room goes flat, like a voice that stopped mid-sentence.
Ask yourself something honest. When was the last time you opened your content calendar and felt anything other than dread?
